card: This PR adds functional tests in tool_bitcoin.py to verify that the Windows bitcoin wrapper process correctly preserves child exit statuses and reports launch failures. It tests that exit codes 0, 1, and -1 are forwarded intact without injecting unexpected stderr output, and verifies that failure to start the child process returns an exit code of 1 with an informative execvp error. The tests specifically guard against a bug in Windows CRT process handling where an exit code of -1 was conflated with process spawn failure. It depends on runtime fixes in #36105.
changed_since_previous: Rebased on updated commits from #36105 with no functional changes to the tests.
evidence: PR description: 'The case worth covering is exit code -1. The first version of the wrapper used _spawnvp(_P_WAIT), which returns -1 both when the spawn fails and when the child started fine and exited with -1, so bitcoin.exe reported a startup error and exited 1 instead of passing -1 through.'
Commit 7395505c2f: 'This detects a bug that was present in the original implementation of the earlier commit "Fix ExecVp on Windows to wait for child process"'
problem: Without dedicated test coverage on Windows, regressions in process execution and exit-code forwarding in the bitcoin wrapper can go unnoticed, such as conflating child exit status -1 with process spawn errors under the Windows CRT.

risk.why: A mistake in the new tests would only cause functional test failures on Windows environments and does not impact node runtime logic.

scope_notes: The PR branch currently includes the prerequisite commits from #36105; the unique changes belonging to this PR are the new test cases added to test/functional/tool_bitcoin.py.
summary: Adds functional tests to tool_bitcoin.py to verify that the Windows bitcoin wrapper preserves child process exit status and reports errors on spawn failure. Specifically, it tests that exit codes 0, 1, and -1 are properly passed through by using cmd.exe as a mock child executable, and confirms that startup errors produce an exit code of 1 with an error message on stderr.
